messages.author: 9b538d9555ff0d8a
messages.subject: Laplace likelihood
parts:
Currently, if someone tries to implement a quantile spatial model using the asymmetric Laplace likelihood, he/she receives the following message:

Model 'laplace' in section 'likelihood' is marked as 'disabled'.
  Usage is not recommended and unsupported.
  You can enable it setting variable 'enable.model.likelihood.laplace'
  to 'TRUE' in environment INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv().
  If you chose to do so, you are on your own.


Could somebody clarify the current issues/problems related to the implementation of the asymmetric Laplace likelihood? 
In which cases can we trust the output by setting enable.model.likelihood.laplace=TRUE ?
Furthermore, any suggestions as to how one can alleviate the problems will be appreciated.

Many thanks,
Yiannis Kamarianakis

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Laplace likelihood
parts:
On Tue, 2015-10-13 at 11:44 -0700, ikam...@asu.edu wrote:
> Currently, if someone tries to implement a quantile spatial model
> using the asymmetric Laplace likelihood, he/she receives the
> following message:
>
> Model 'laplace' in section 'likelihood' is marked as 'disabled'.
> Usage is not recommended and unsupported.
> You can enable it setting variable
> 'enable.model.likelihood.laplace'
> to 'TRUE' in environment INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv().
> If you chose to do so, you are on your own.
>
>
> Could somebody clarify the current issues/problems related to the
> implementation of the asymmetric Laplace likelihood?
> In which cases can we trust the output by setting
> enable.model.likelihood.laplace=TRUE ?
> Furthermore, any suggestions as to how one can alleviate the problems
> will be appreciated.

Hi,

the main issue is that the double laplace has zero second deriviate of
the log likelihood, although there is an overall 'curvature'. this
means that there is no local information in the likelihood about the
variance, just the mean. there are also problems with the numerical
optimizer in this case.

I doubt that laplace approximations are adequate for this case, and
something else must be done. OR, there is some empirical evidence that
the estimates achived are good (mean and especially the variance).

For these reasons, it is disabled.

It is possible to do parametric quantile regression instead, of
course...

Best
H

messages.author: 0f442fa6eadc8950
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Laplace likelihood
parts:
Many thanks Havard.
A quick clarification:

when you write "It is possible to do parametric quantile regression instead, of
course..."

I believe that you do not mean that it is safe to estimate models like:

enable.model.likelihood.laplace=TRUE

formula.inla.sp  =    ILT ~ 1 +TAWSS + OSI + RRT  + f(ID1, model="bym",graph=adjn1)

mod.linear.sp.q90 = inla(formula.inla.sp,  data=pat1, family = "laplace" , control.compute=list(dic=T), control.predictor= list(compute=T),
control.family= list(alpha=0.9, gamma=2,epsilon=0.01) )

What I wrote above is a parametric model but I believe that the explanation in your previous message applies in this case as well.

Many thanks and congrats for your work.

Yiannis

Hi,

I mean more that we define the linear predictor as a certain quantile
instead of as the mean (in the Gaussian case f.ex). this is a 'new
likelihood' as the linear predictor enters differently in the
likelihood. 

Anyone that has some experience with this?

Best
H
